newsitem.title: GERMANY: West, east German inflation converge in October.
newsitem.headline: West, east German inflation converge in October.

text.p: Inflation in former communist east Germany converged in October for the first time with the 1.5 percent annual price growth in the west, final data published on Monday by the Federal Statistics Office showed.

The data were not revised after the earlier release of provisional inflation estimates for October based on four west German states, leaving the overall consumer price index steady in relation to September.

Prices of personal equipment fell by 1.5 percent in October against September, while food and drink was also lower by 0.2 percent. But rents and energy were up by 0.5 percent -- with higher oil prices driving up heating oil prices sharply.
On a year-on-year basis, rents and energy were again the main motor behind price increases, with most other categories coming in below the headline inflation figure.
